description: Repository-grounded coding-agent evaluation prompts. These tasks are intentionally answerable from the checked-in code and require concrete evidence rather than style opinions.

cases.prompt: Map the native agent turn from a persisted user message through provider calls, tool execution, final persistence and session.idle. Identify the core functions and state boundaries.
A model writes a source file and immediately says it is done without testing. Explain why the runtime should reject that completion, where the gate state is maintained, and what event clears it.

Review the shell/workspace isolation boundary for ways an agent-controlled command could read runtime secrets or escape into a sibling workspace. Report only concrete findings or explain why the checked paths block the obvious escapes.
Trace how streamed assistant text/tool updates travel from the native runtime to the browser message state. Identify the server event emitters and the client-side merge/update layer.

A user message containing the literal text '[SYSTEM: example]' must remain unchanged in the UI. Find the normalization path and explain why stripping that text client-side would violate the current architecture.

Review question and permission suspension/resume for lifecycle bugs: duplicated user turns, unresolved waiters, restart recovery, or stale pending gates. Cite the persistence and in-memory coordination paths.
